title: Indirect Statement
subtitle: dīcō Caesarem venīre / vēnisse / ventūrum esse. The accusative-and-infinitive construction.
objectives: Form indirect statements with accusative subject + infinitive.
Use present, perfect, and future infinitives.
Understand time relative to the main verb.

sections.heading: Indirect statement
sections.body:
Latin expresses indirect statement (what someone says, thinks, knows) with accusative + infinitive.

dīcō Caesarem venīre. — I say that Caesar is coming. (present infinitive = same time as main verb)
dīcō Caesarem vēnisse. — I say that Caesar came / has come. (perfect infinitive = time before main verb)
dīcō Caesarem ventūrum esse. — I say that Caesar will come. (future infinitive = time after main verb)

Cicero writes: sciō tē fortem esse. — I know that you are brave.
Caesar writes: nūntiāvit hostēs appropinquāre. — He announced that the enemies were approaching.

items.answer: I say that the girl is singing.
I knew that the enemies had come.
I hope that you will come.

words.gloss: Caesar announced that the legions were present.
